name: Periosteal Resonance Targeting Drone PRTD-5 'Knuckle'
description:
The PRTD-5 is a close-support targeting and area-denial drone developed by ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS under a joint contract with military medical research divisions. It operates by emitting narrow-band low-frequency acoustic pulses precisely tuned to periosteal resonance frequencies — the vibrational signature of the membrane sheathing bone. At its standard operational distance of 2–6 meters, these pulses produce deep, nauseating ache in weight-bearing joints: knees, hips, ankles, and wrists. The sensation is not structural damage but reads to the nervous system as imminent catastrophic fracture, producing involuntary protective responses including crouching, freezing, and gait collapse.

The PRTD-5 is distinguished from simpler acoustic deterrents by its precision tracking suite. An onboard millimeter-wave radar maps the target's skeletal geometry in real time, allowing the drone to adjust its emission frequency to match individual bone density — thicker cortical bone requires lower frequencies and higher amplitude. This adaptive tuning means the effect is not trivially countered by body armor or padding, which attenuates higher-frequency acoustic weapons but does relatively little against the PRTD-5's deep-penetration range. The drone is roughly the size and shape of a softball, matte gray, and nearly silent in flight.

ACTARUS markets it officially as a non-lethal crowd management tool for use by licensed security contractors. The military variant, designated PRTD-5M, operates at amplitudes that cause genuine microfracture accumulation over extended exposure — a detail absent from the civilian product documentation.
specifications:
dimensions: 11 cm diameter sphere
weight: 0.62 kg
operational range: 2–6 m standard, 1–3 m PRTD-5M
frequency range: 18–34 Hz adaptive
target acquisition: Millimeter-wave radar, 0.3 s lock time
effect onset: 2–4 seconds post-lock
flight ceiling: 25 m
battery life: 55 minutes continuous operation
noise signature: < 28 dB at 3 m
countermeasures: Acoustic damping exoskeleton underlayer, rated ADA-3 or higher
tactical_use: Security contractors deploy PRTD-5 units to control movement through checkpoints, suppress crowd rushes, and immobilize fleeing individuals without physical pursuit. In tighter operational contexts — hostage rescue, precision arrest — teams use it to collapse a target's mobility before entry, eliminating the risk of armed resistance during the first seconds of contact. Military units using the 5M variant employ extended loiter patterns over fortified positions, accumulating microfracture damage in defenders over hours of siege.
cultural_context: ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS maintains careful public messaging around the PRTD-5, emphasizing its non-lethal classification and medical research origins. In GLMZ, it has nonetheless become synonymous with a specific kind of institutional brutality — the kind that leaves no marks. Human rights organizations document its use in labor disputes and protest suppression, where its effects are invisible on post-incident medical scans. The drone's softball-like silhouette has been adopted as an ironic logo by several labor activist groups, printed on shirts alongside the phrase 'non-lethal.'
known_users: ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS licensed security contractors
Black market resellers supplying mid-tier criminal organizations
story_hooks: A licensed PRTD-5 unit was used during a labor action at an OUROBOROS ENERGY processing facility. Three workers sustained injuries consistent with PRTD-5M exposure — microfracture patterns that shouldn't appear on civilian hardware. Someone swapped the firmware, and ARCTURUS wants it buried.

A PRTD-5 has been loitering above a specific intersection in the market district for six days, tracking and harassing the same elderly shopkeeper. It's licensed to a shell company that dissolved four years ago.
The party is hired to retrieve a PRTD-5M from a military crash site before ARCTURUS' recovery team arrives. The drone is still active, still tracking, and the crash site is not empty.

physical_description.visual_profile: A compact sphere barely larger than a closed fist, with a nearly invisible profile in flight. The silhouette is deceptively simple — a smooth ball with minimal visual indication of its acoustic weaponry. At rest, it resembles precision sports equipment or a sensor node more than a weapon, which is intentional.
physical_description.dimensions: 11 cm diameter sphere; no protruding elements or appendages
physical_description.weight_description: Substantial but balanced — 0.62 kg feels dense in the palm, concentrated mass without awkward weight distribution. Drones of this size usually feel hollow; the Knuckle feels purposefully compact.
physical_description.primary_material: Reinforced polymer composite core with acoustic dampening matrix shell; titanium resonance chamber assembly visible only under disassembly
physical_description.finish: Matte gray anodized coating, industrial-grade non-reflective — designed to minimize visual acquisition at operational distance
physical_description.color_scheme: Flat military gray primary; minimal accent — only small ARCTURUS Defense Solutions embossed logo and serial plate in gunmetal
physical_description.grip_texture: Smooth, slightly tacky polymer exterior with micro-grip texture to prevent slipping during launch or retrieval
distinctive_features: Hairline seams where acoustic emitter array sits flush with exterior — visible only at close inspection
Miniature LED status indicator (amber/green) recessed into one hemisphere, barely perceptible until powered
Subtle thermal venting ports arranged in symmetric pattern around equator
Serial plate stamped with ARCTURUS logo and 'PRTD-5' designation
Barely audible high-frequency chirp when powered — calibration tone, sub-30dB
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS embossed in small sans-serif font on one pole of sphere; serial number and regulatory compliance stamps on opposite pole; '6-YEAR WARRANTY' micro-printed on datasheets but not on physical unit
physical_description.condition_typical: Civilian units maintain pristine finish; field-deployed PRTD-5M variants show scuffing on the acoustic dampening shell, minor impact marks from rough extraction protocols, possible carbon scoring from sustained thermal cycling
